title: Dragon's Elemental Siege — Shader Spell System
description: A translucent dragon hovers above a miniature city. The user crafts elemental shader spells by combining color channels, distortion parameters, and glow intensities across multiple linked controls, then casts them onto city buildings to transform their material appearance. A conservation law ensures total shader energy is fixed — boosting one spell weakens others — and full undo/redo tracks every step.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads DragonAttenuation.glb hovering 6 units above VirtualCity.glb placed at the origin. Use OrbitControls with the camera at (12,10,12) looking at (0,2,0). Add a hemisphere light and a warm directional light casting shadows. Implement a custom ShaderMaterial spell system with these requirements: 1) Create a UI panel with 4 spell slots, each having three coupled sliders: Hue (0-360), Distortion strength (0-1), and Glow intensity (0-2). Enforce a CONSERVATION LAW: the sum of all 12 slider values across all 4 slots is capped at a fixed energy budget of 12.0. Adjusting any slider automatically scales down other sliders proportionally to maintain the budget. 2) The dragon uses a custom fragment shader with uniforms for subsurface-style attenuation color tinted by the currently selected spell's hue, plus vertex displacement in the vertex shader driven by the distortion parameter. 3) Clicking a building in the city (via raycasting) applies the active spell: the building's material is replaced with a custom ShaderMaterial whose fragment shader uses the spell's hue for a color wash, distortion for UV warping, and glow for an additive rim-light effect. Each building tracks which spell was applied. 4) Implement full undo/redo with Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y that reverts both slider states and building material assignments. Store at least 20 history states. 5) A spell selector (buttons 1-4) sets the active spell; the dragon's shader updates in real-time to preview the active spell. 6) Display a top bar showing remaining energy budget and active spell number. The interaction flow requires: selecting spells, tuning 3 parameters each across 4 spells under conservation, clicking 3+ buildings, and using undo/redo — totaling 10-14 meaningful steps. Use GLSL noise for distortion and Fresnel approximation for glow in the custom shaders.
